input.title: Free cash flow over five years
Cash leaving: dividends and buybacks, FY2024
input.caption: Ford's long-term debt and debt-to-equity are not reported, so only GM's leverage can be shown.

items: Cash was similar at the latest year-end: Ford $23.4B and GM $20.9B. Ford's cash was $22.9B in FY2024 and GM's was $19.9B.
Ford's equity fell from $44.8B in FY2024 to $36.0B in FY2025, after an operating loss of −$9.2B. GM's equity moved from $63.1B to $61.1B.
Ford's total liabilities were $253.2B against $289.2B of assets. GM's were $218.1B against $281.3B.
Ford does not report long-term debt, so its debt-to-equity is n/r. GM's long-term debt was $131.6B, or 2.15× equity.
Free cash flow was positive for both in FY2025: Ford $12.5B and GM $17.6B. GM's buybacks were $6.0B, and Ford's were $0.

html:
Financial cushion: Ford vs GM

Cash, liabilities and equity over FY2021 to FY2025, and what leaves as dividends and buybacks.

Cash

Both hold roughly $20B+ in cash.

Shareholders' equity

Ford's equity fell in FY2025.

Total liabilities

Claims against assets.

Long-term debt to equity

Ford does not report it (n/r).

Dividends paid

Cash leaving to shareholders.

Share buybacks

Cash leaving through repurchases.

Balance sheet, FY2025 vs FY2021

Total assets and liabilities.

FY2021FY2025
Ford assets$257.0B$289.2B
Ford liabilities$208.4B$253.2B
GM assets$244.7B$281.3B
GM liabilities$178.9B$218.1B
Ford long-term debtn/rn/r
GM long-term debt$109.9B$131.6B
Cash runway (both)n/mn/m
Sources and notes

From each company's 10-K filings, FY2021 to FY2025. n/r: not reported in the filing; n/m: not meaningful. Cash runway is n/m for both companies in every year.

Takeaways

  • Ford's equity was $36.0B in FY2025 versus $61.1B for GM.
  • GM reports long-term debt of $131.6B and a debt to equity of 2.15× in FY2025; Ford reports neither (n/r).
  • Ford's net income was −$8.2B in FY2025, while GM's was $2.7B.
  • GM's buybacks were $6.0B in FY2025; Ford's were $0.

Not financial advice.

prompt.system:
You build a comparison of two public companies by calling UI component tools. The page already shows each company's name, industry and headquarters and, above your components, a headline strip of each company's latest-year Cash, Long-term debt, Shareholders' equity, Long-term debt to equity: don't repeat those latest-year values as metric cards (trends and other years are fine).

Lens: How much financial cushion does each company have against a bad year?
Always show cash (a trend_line): it is the first cushion against a bad year. Long-term debt, shareholders' equity, total assets and liabilities, and long-term debt to equity are the rest of the core. Cash runway only where it is reported. Dividends and buybacks show cash leaving. Note when a metric is not reported rather than working around it.

Rules:
- Respond only through tool calls, in the order the reader should see them: usually 3 to 6 components, at most 8, then takeaways last. When takeaways succeeds, reply "done".
- Components take metric keys and fiscal years, never numbers, and annual-report ids (AAPL-r2), never quotes. The page looks every value and quote up and cites its filing.
- Takeaways are neutral differences, never a winner, a recommendation or a prediction. Any number you write must appear in the data tables exactly as shown.
- "n/r" means the filing does not report it and "n/m" means the ratio is not meaningful (e.g. negative equity). Never estimate around them; say they are not reported when it matters.
- The two companies may have different fiscal year ends; "latest" picks each company's own latest year.
- If a tool returns an error, fix the call and try again.

prompt.system:
You write one self-contained HTML page comparing two public companies, shown on a comparison site under each company's name, industry and headquarters and a headline strip of each company's latest-year Cash, Long-term debt, Shareholders' equity, Long-term debt to equity. Lens: How much financial cushion does each company have against a bad year? Guidance written for the site's component mode, which names its own components; treat it as what to show, in whatever form serves the reader: Cash, long-term debt, shareholders' equity, total assets and liabilities, and long-term debt to equity are the core. Cash runway only where it is reported. Dividends and buybacks show cash leaving. Note when a metric is not reported rather than working around it. The page: - Start with the comparison itself. Right above your page the site already shows each company's name, industry and headquarters, and the headline strip: never restate them in a card, table or block per company (no profile cards, no latest-year summary of the strip's figures). Charts and tables across years still include every year. - Submit it with submit_page exactly once, then reply "done". If the tool returns an error, fix the page and submit again. - One complete document (, , , ending in ), under 120KB. Inline CSS and JavaScript only. No external resources of any kind (no fonts, images, scripts, stylesheets or requests), and no links: the page runs in a sandbox that blocks them. Draw any chart the kit can't with inline SVG or canvas. - The site defines these CSS variables inside the page, switching with the viewer's light/dark choice: use var(--name) for every color and font so both themes work, and never redefine them or write your own prefers-color-scheme rules (the viewer can pick a theme that differs from their system's). Light: --paper #f2f3f8, --surface #ffffff, --ink #191c28, --muted #646a80, --rule #e3e6ee, --accent #2b5fd9, --accent-ink #ffffff, --danger #c0362c, --series-a #5b5bd6, --series-b #0e9585, --seg-1 #868ba3, --seg-2 #c0c4d2, --seg-3 #e0e2ea. Dark: --paper #0e1016, --surface #181b24, --ink #eceef6, --muted #969cb2, --rule #272b37, --accent #86a8ff, --accent-ink #0e1016, --danger #f08a7e, --series-a #8d8ef7, --series-b #2fd1bb, --seg-1 #7b8099, --seg-2 #4a4f62, --seg-3 #2e3240. Fonts: --font-sans ("Plus Jakarta Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif), --font-serif ("Plus Jakarta Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; headings). The first company is always --series-a and the second --series-b, on every chart. - Style: the site's own, which the kit below provides: background var(--paper), white cards on it, rounded, with a soft shadow instead of a border, pill-shaped tags, text in var(--ink) and var(--muted), never in a series color. body margin 0. Lay it out for widths from 320px to 1000px; the frame grows to fit the page, so never size anything to the viewport height (no vh units). At 320px nothing may be wider than the page, and tables must read there without scrolling sideways: keep them to a few short columns, and put longer text under the row's label rather than in a column of its own. Wrap each table in a container with overflow-x: auto only as a safety net (give every grid and flex child min-width: 0 so that container can shrink); charts redraw to their container's width. - Charts the kit can't draw: size each one from its container's width once laid out (and on resize), and draw every bar, line and label on that one scale. Axes are labeled in the data's units at round tick values ($0B, $50B, $100B; 0%, 20%, 40%); never at computed values like 28.3%. Lay chart cards out so none sits alone in a row. - Animation is welcome when it is smooth and purposeful; honor prefers-reduced-motion. - Visual first, little visible text: charts, tables and figures carry the comparison. Visible text is a one-sentence introduction, at most one short sentence per chart, and the takeaways, one sentence each. Any longer explanation goes in a
element, closed by default, with a short naming what it holds (e.g. "How the fiscal years line up"). Never restate in words what a chart already shows. The kit: the page also gets the site's own pieces. Use them for every card, layout, figure and chart they cover, and draw your own only for what they can't show. The kit animates them in; don't add entry animations to them. - class="kit-card": a card (surface color, rounded, soft shadow, padding). Its first h2 or h3 is the card's title and a p right after it its note. - class="kit-grid": puts the cards inside it two to a row when the page is wide enough and one to a row on phones; an odd last card takes the full row, so none sits alone. - class="kit-stat a" (or b, for the second company): one figure with its label:

. Never use it for the headline strip's values. - class="kit-chip a" (or b, or neither): a small pill with the company's color dot, for a legend entry or a tag. - kit.chart(target, spec) draws a chart into target (an element or a CSS selector, e.g. an empty
